title: Milestone 2 · Finish bookings and recover replies
baseline: Baseline: fresh milestone 1 edaddef (atomic holds; 33 tests)

columns.title: Recover a lost reply
columns.today: Creation cannot be recovered without its ID.
columns.detail: Retry the same request key and seat set to recover one reservation across restarts.

columns.title: Complete the booking
columns.detail: Confirm by reservation ID so the whole group stays booked.

columns.title: Release an unwanted hold
columns.detail: Cancel by ID so every seat becomes available to another caller.

columns.title: One key, one selection
columns.detail: Same key plus reordered seats is the same request; different seats return 409.

columns.title: Stable terminal outcomes
columns.detail: Repeat the same terminal action safely. Confirm after cancel, or cancel after confirm, returns 409.

columns.title: Keep existing reservations
columns.detail: Upgrade in place; retain IDs, selections and claims. Existing clients can still omit a key.

columns.title: Complete, exclusive groups
columns.detail: Atomic allocation and one active owner per seat remain required.

columns.title: Booking client
columns.detail: Generate and retain a request_key before sending; reuse it for recovery.

columns.title: Movie Seats API
columns.detail: Expose confirmation and return the updated booking state.

columns.title: Reservation service
columns.detail: Own lifecycle decisions and release only the cancelled reservation’s claims.

columns.title: SQLite engine
columns.detail: Persist request-key mappings in the same transaction as successful allocation.

columns.title: Competing workers
columns.detail: Independent connections serialize writes through the same local database file.

columns.title: Startup migration
columns.detail: Atomically add request mappings and advance to version 2 without rebuilding reservations.

columns.title: Uvicorn + local file
columns.detail: One host; operator retains MOVIE_SEATS_DB across restarts.

columns.title: domain.py · request identity
columns.detail: Accept 1–128 ASCII key characters; canonical seat order defines selection equivalence.

columns.title: domain.py · transition
columns.detail: held -> confirmed/cancelled; matching terminal state is a no-op; opposite state conflicts.

columns.title: db.py · complete
columns.detail: Read state under the write lock; update state and remove claims together on cancellation.

columns.title: db.py · hold
columns.today: Each call allocates a new hold or fails.
columns.detail: Check a key before availability; return a Creation result distinguishing first creation from replay.

columns.title: api.py
columns.detail: First creation 201; replay 200. Action success/repeat 200; conflicting operation 409.

columns.title: db.py · initialize
columns.detail: Create requests table, retain all existing rows, and commit user_version=2 last.

columns.title: Selection + health handlers
columns.detail: Retain strict selection validation, page, health, atomic holds and lookup.

columns.title: request_key
columns.detail: Caller-generated [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*; same key survives lost replies and restarts.

columns.title: POST confirm
columns.detail: Return confirmed with the same ID and seats. Repetition preserves the result.

columns.title: POST cancel
columns.detail: Return cancelled with original seats; remove only that reservation’s active claims.

columns.title: Key replay / mismatch
columns.detail: 200 with current reservation state for equivalent input; 409 for another seat set.

columns.title: Concurrent completion
columns.detail: Confirm versus cancel: one terminal result wins; the incompatible request receives 409.

columns.title: Keyless creation
columns.detail: Existing body {seats:[A3,A4]} remains valid, but has no creation-replay guarantee.

columns.title: GET screening / reservation
columns.detail: Expose confirmed and cancelled reservation states; confirmed seats remain unavailable.

columns.title: Request identity
columns.detail: requests maps one key to one reservation ID; keep the mapping after completion.

columns.title: Confirmed reservation
columns.detail: Keep the original seat list and all active claims; no later cancellation or reopening.

columns.title: Cancelled reservation
columns.detail: Preserve ID and requested seats; delete current claims so a new request can own them.

columns.title: Key binding transaction
columns.detail: Insert key only with successful allocation. Failed validation or conflict does not consume it.

columns.title: Terminal state + claims
columns.detail: State change and claim effects share one transaction. Repeated cancellation cannot release a new owner.

columns.title: Version-2 database
columns.detail: Add mappings; old holds remain unkeyed. Refuse newer schemas without deleting data.

columns.title: Immutable requested selection
columns.detail: Original reservation_seats rows survive every transition and support replay equivalence.

columns.title: Lost-reply recovery
columns.detail: Discard creation reply; restart; retry key and recover exactly the original ID.

columns.title: Lifecycle matrix
columns.detail: held/confirmed/cancelled × confirm/cancel; repeats succeed, opposite finals conflict.

columns.title: Release + reallocation
columns.detail: Cancel A3+A4; new key can hold them. Repeating old cancel cannot release the new claims.

columns.title: Replay binding checks
columns.detail: Reordered seats replay; mismatch conflicts; failed request leaves key free; cancelled replay cannot rehold.

columns.title: Racing operations
columns.detail: Same-key race creates one ID. Confirm/cancel race leaves one valid terminal outcome.

columns.title: Upgrade preservation
columns.detail: Frozen SQL from fresh milestone 1 retains its ID, seats and claims; old hold can complete.

columns.title: Retained guarantees
columns.detail: Run earlier validation, rollback, contention, health and process-restart checks.

nodes.title: Booking client
nodes.detail: POST A3+A4 with key party-17; retain the key before sending.

nodes.title: Movie Seats API
nodes.detail: Validate key; expose completion routes; return 201 creation or 200 replay.

nodes.title: Lifecycle policy
nodes.detail: Held may finish; repeat the same final is safe; conflicting final returns 409.

nodes.title: Reservation service
nodes.detail: Look up key before availability. Compare original seats. Complete only under the same write lock.

nodes.title: SQLite engine
nodes.detail: Commit key + hold together. On cancellation, commit state + claim release together.

notes: REPLAY · Key party-17 resolves the original ID before checking availability. A replay reports current state; it never creates another hold.
CONFIRM · held -> confirmed keeps all claims. Confirm again returns the same booking. Cancel after confirmation returns 409.
CANCEL · held -> cancelled removes that ID’s claims. Cancel again does nothing, even after someone else acquires those seats.
UPGRADE · The fresh version-1 fixture keeps its ID, A3+A4 selection and claims. A new requests table supplies future retry identity.
COMPATIBILITY · Omitted request_key retains milestone-1 behavior. Requiring a key would break those clients with 422; this proposal avoids that break.

summary: A key identifies a creation request, not a new attempt. A terminal reservation retains its history; only current claims determine availability.
